units: Figures are conceptual diagrams and visual representations of authority dynamics.
Authority decay curve illustrates persistent contradiction, exponential decline, and half-life.
Authority flow depicts environment -> observation -> residual -> attribution -> authority update -> future computation.
Adaptive selection landscape depicts mechanism population -> outcomes -> empirical pressure -> authority redistribution -> new distribution.
Figures should emphasize causal direction, dynamic change, and empirical grounding.
Phase-transition, competition-simulation, half-life, restoration, stability, and baseline-comparison figures are proposed future work.
Conceptual figures are not empirical plots or implementation diagrams.
Depicts mechanism population -> empirical pressure -> authority redistribution -> new mechanism distribution.
Illustrative authority values A=0.8, B=0.6, C=0.4 become 0.9, 0.2, 0.7 after schematic success, failure, and improvement.
Illustrative numeric values are schematic, not reported measurements.
Selection is described as variation -> competition -> environment -> residual -> authority update -> new distribution.
Retrieval strategies or generated abstractions are examples of competing mechanisms.
Unit of selection is causal influence over representations, paths, structures, and strategies.
Authority dynamics selects existing mechanisms; long-term adaptation additionally requires variation and creation.
Delta mathcal A approximately 0 under viable stable conditions; environmental change should move the landscape.
Fixed authority with repeated failure is presented as non-adaptive.
Unrestricted or random redistribution is presented as unstable; correction and stability are both required.
Proposed experiment asks whether dynamic internal selection outperforms output or memory-only adaptation.
Visualizes exponential authority attenuation under persistent empirical contradiction.
Schematic authority-time curve highlights a 0.5 authority half-life level.
X-axis is time or correction cycles; Y-axis is mechanism authority A_i(t).
Phi_R(e_t,m_i) is attributed empirical contradiction pressure.
beta controls response speed; higher beta is associated with shorter half-life and higher instability risk.
Failure reduces future dominance rather than instantly deleting a mechanism.
Linear, threshold, and exponential variants are proposed for conceptual comparison.
Validation asks whether reducing contradicted mechanism influence improves long-horizon adaptation.
Curve is conceptual; no measured decay series is reported.
Depicts reality -> residual -> attribution -> authority change -> future behavior.
External conditions are framed as final source of selection pressure.
Observed outcome y_t provides opportunity for correction.
Updated authority changes which mechanisms shape future reasoning.
Error detection plus memory update with unchanged mechanism is presented as a repeated-failure pattern.
External evidence -> internal mechanism change is described as a core adaptive requirement.
Source asserts RAHU tests contradiction detection, attribution, authority reduction, future behavior change, and recurrence.
Hypothesis: intelligence includes the ability for contradicted mechanisms to lose causal control.
Diagram is conceptual and does not establish the depicted causal pathway empirically.
Project is framed as a testable framework to be refined, challenged, and potentially falsified.
Central hypothesis: empirical reality must be able to modify causal influence of structures responsible for future behavior.
Invites alternative derivations, proofs or counterexamples, formal improvements, missing assumptions, and comparisons.
Invites benchmark environments, simulations, ablations, and comparisons measuring adaptation speed, recurrence, stability, persistence, and redistribution.
Invites attacks on mechanism attribution, causal meaning of authority, exponential law, redundancy with existing methods, and framework failure modes.
Any future implementation should be documented, reproducible, tested, and used to test theory rather than optimize only benchmark performance.
Changes should identify what changed, why, and which assumption changed.
Extensions should define measurable variables, expected outcomes, and failure conditions.
Authority, confidence, probability, reward, memory, and correctness should remain distinct.
Contributions should provide description, validation evidence or arguments, and limitations.
Discussion should emphasize evidence, formal reasoning, empirical validation, predictions, and falsification.
Purpose is to investigate whether empirical regulation of mechanisms improves adaptive intelligence, not defend a fixed formulation.
Contribution policy describes desired future evidence and reproducibility; it is not itself an execution or reproduction record.
Title: The Law of Adaptive Authority Dynamics; author Björn Janson; version 0.1.0; release date 2026-07-31; CC-BY-4.0.
Citation abstract describes empirical feedback regulating causal influence, exponential attenuation, and viability-gated restoration.
CITATION.cff labels the work type as software.
Metadata type software does not establish executable implementation on the frozen source surface.
